briefing.title: Briefing after cycle 012 — what the world is pressing on

question: Which of these two should the world act on first, in the coming year?

matters.title: Ebola in Congo, still running
matters.gist: The Bundibugyo outbreak in eastern Congo keeps rising nearly six months on, with cases in Kenya and Nigeria and no approved vaccine for this strain.

matters.title: One in ten below three dollars a day
matters.gist: Extreme poverty barely moves: about one in ten people live on less than three dollars a day, rising in one region and high in another.

matters.title: Interest before hospitals
matters.gist: In much of the developing world, governments now spend more on interest to creditors than on health or on education.

matters.title: Three quarters of the world's wealth
matters.gist: The richest tenth holds most of the world's wealth, and the poorer half holds almost none of it.

matters.title: Five companies, most of the machines
matters.gist: Five cloud companies own most of the world's computing power for AI, and their share grew through 2025.

matters.title: Three in four people under autocracy
matters.gist: Most of the world's people now live in autocracies, and global freedom has declined for two decades in a row.

matters.title: The warmest October, with El Niño rising
matters.gist: The world has just had its warmest October on record, and a very strong El Niño is still building in the Pacific.

matters.title: COP31 opens on a 2.8-degree path
matters.gist: The climate summit in Antalya opens while current policies still point to far more warming than the Paris goal.

matters.title: The air that kills millions
matters.gist: Air pollution is among the largest causes of early death in the world, most of it in low- and middle-income countries.

matters.title: Appeals less than half funded
matters.gist: With two months of the year left, the world's humanitarian appeals have received less than half of what they asked for.
